lines.text: Everything so far has been about moving bytes. Now what can they do? They become pictures.
Your screen is a window. And every window is just pixels - tiny squares of light the computer paints fresh, every frame.
The GPU takes those instructions and turns them into geometry. Millions of triangles, rendered in real time.
The CPU prepares the scene. The GPU executes it. Together they translate bytes into motion.
Shaders run on the GPU. They decide color. Light. Texture. What the eye will see.
The frame buffer fills. Vertices become pixels. Triangles become images.
And the loop repeats - billions of times per second - turning code into motion.
Every pixel on your screen is the result of instructions. Code became light.
From bytes to pixels. That is the whole stack. One step out of five.
Next: how we make it beautiful. Color, light, and the frame.
